response.query: What selection thresholds from survey scores (e.g., top/bottom quartile, >75th percentile) should trigger qualitative follow-up interviews?
response.answer: For qualitative follow-up interviews, select survey scores from the top 25th percentile or bottom 25th percentile to trigger deeper exploration. Aim for a sample size that reaches saturation, typically around 30 to 70 interviews.

results.title: A Guide to Sample Sizes in Qualitative UX Research
results.content: A guide to determining sample size for saturation in qualitative research (interviews, usability testing, etc) with our data-backed sample size formula. At the very least, I’ve created a formula for estimating the sample size you need to reach saturation for 7 different qualitative methods—and I feel pretty good about its application in User Research. So, in order to facilitate efficient, decision-driven research, the sample size recommendations in our calculator are based on *meaning* *saturation* for different study types wherever possible. Marketing research firm IntoTheMinds offers an interview study size calculator with recommendations partially based on Marshall et al (2013). “Beyond the Five-User Assumption: Benefits of Increased Sample Sizes in Usability Testing.” *Behavior Research Methods, Instruments, & Computers*, 35(3), 379–383. Estimating Sample Sizes in Focus Group Research.” *Qualitative Health Research*, 29(10), 1483–1496.
